extracted.intended_audience: Researchers/authors, reviewers, editors and staff submitting to or handling manuscripts for Frontiers journals
extracted.subtask_description: Publisher-level policies and ethics guidance for preparing, submitting, reviewing, and post-publishing handling of manuscripts submitted to Frontiers journals. Covers authorship, data and image integrity, clinical trial/reporting requirements, conflicts of interest, peer-review conduct, open data, and post-publication corrections/retractions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorship attribution: named authors vs contributors
rubrics_metrics.description: All individuals contributing to academic work must be clearly defined as either named authors (published in the byline and detailed in the contributions statement) or contributors (credited in acknowledgments). Only individuals who have made a substantial contribution to the research and writing of the manuscript may be listed as authors. Any arrangement involving payment or compensation in exchange for authorship without contribution is unethical and prohibited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must ensure all contributors, their institutions, and precise contributions are listed correctly. Contributors who do not meet authorship criteria must be acknowledged with their permission. Frontiers may investigate suspected authorship manipulation and contact institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author affiliations
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must list the institution at the time the research was conducted as their primary affiliation. Further affiliations can be listed subsequently in the submission system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing false, fabricated, or knowingly inaccurate affiliations (including listing a former or unaffiliated institution for prestige) may breach publishing ethics and trigger investigations involving the relevant institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualifying for named authorship (ICMJE criteria)
rubrics_metrics.description: Frontiers follows ICMJE guidelines: to qualify for authorship, individuals should meet criteria including (a) acquisition, analysis, or interpretation of data; (b) drafting the work or revising it critically for important intellectual content; (c) providing approval for publication; and (d) agreeing to be accountable for all aspects of the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To comply, each co-author must have participated in writing the original draft and/or critically reviewed/edited the manuscript. Those not meeting these criteria should be included in acknowledgments; it is the submitting author's responsibility to obtain written approval from those acknowledged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author contribution statements using CRediT taxonomy
rubrics_metrics.description: During submission, submitting authors must specify each co-author's contributions using the CRediT (Contributor Roles Taxonomy) roles; an author contributions statement is then automatically generated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CRediT roles include: Conceptualization; Data curation; Formal analysis; Funding acquisition; Investigation; Methodology; Project administration; Resources; Software; Supervision; Validation; Visualization; Writing – original draft; Writing – review & editing. Example contribution string is provided in policy. To comply with Frontiers and ICMJE, co-authors must have participated in drafting or critical review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corresponding author responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: The corresponding author takes primary responsibility for communication with the journal during submission, peer review, and publication; ensuring submission adheres to journal requirements (authorship details, ethics approval, trial registration, COI declaration); and being available post-publication to respond to queries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corresponding authors should ensure all required statements/documents are provided during submission and be responsive after publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Changes in authorship policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The submitting author must include all co-authors during submission; requests to change the author list are considered only in exceptional circumstances and must adhere to Frontiers' authorship policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorship changes after submission must be made via an authorship change request form and are rarely approved post-acceptance. Frontiers may contact authors' institutions if manipulation is suspected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusive language policy
rubrics_metrics.description: All submitted and published material must use culturally sensitive, inclusive language that is free from terminology that could be interpreted as hostile or offensive based on group differences (ethnicity, gender, sexuality, age, health, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors, reviewers, editors, and staff share responsibility. Editors/reviewers may suggest alternative language; Frontiers may modify language pre- or post-publication in exceptional circumstances to ensure compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusive image policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Images selected for publication should be ethically informed, culturally sensitive, contextually appropriate, and reflective of global diversity, avoiding stereotypes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider cultural sensitivity, social impact, representation and relevance. Editors may request alternative images; adhere to legal guidelines on image reuse and provide appropriate declarations where control images are reused.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality and duplicate submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Frontiers publishes only original content; manuscripts must not have been previously published or be under consideration elsewhere (in whole or in part). Submitting the same manuscript to multiple journals is duplicate submission and considered misconduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If previously submitted elsewhere, Frontiers will only consider the manuscript if it has been definitively rejected by other publisher(s) at the time of submission. Authors must disclose related publications and cite related material where appropriate; preprints are permitted under the preprint policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fabrication and falsification prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: Fabrication (making up data) and falsification (intentional misrepresentation or manipulation of data/images) are prohibited. Manuscripts produced by paper mills or fake-paper factories are not acceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frontiers uses proactive checks to reject suspicious manuscripts prior to peer review. Evidence of fabrication/falsification will lead to rejection, retraction, and possible institutional reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Redundant publication and 'salami slicing' policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Redundant publication occurs when the same or very similar research is published more than once by the same or overlapping author groups; adding small amounts of new data to an existing published paper without substantive novelty is unethical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For work that previously appeared as conference papers, authors must expand substantially (rule of thumb: at least 30% original content) and cite/acknowledge the conference. All submissions are screened for redundancy; disclose related material and explain how the manuscript adds to the literature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plagiarism and text overlap screening
rubrics_metrics.description: All manuscripts are screened for textual overlap using CrossCheck (iThenticate). Plagiarism (presenting previously published work as original) and unacceptable text-reuse will render manuscripts ineligible for publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original wording taken from other publications must appear in quotation marks with appropriate citations. This applies to others' works and the author's own previously published material (self-plagiarism).

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted ethical text re-use categories (theses, conferences, blogs, preprints, translations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Frontiers allows certain re-use under specified conditions: theses/dissertations (if only the thesis has the content and university policy allows); conference papers (require substantial new material, permission where needed); blogs (must be declared in acknowledgments); preprints (allowed with conditions); translations (explicit permission and declaration).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thesis content should be cited and noted in acknowledgements; conference-origin manuscripts should add substantial original content (≈30%) and cite/acknowledge the conference; preprints must be declared and cannot contain Frontiers branding after submission; translations must declare original publication and permissions, and may be checked for overlap.

rubrics_metrics.name: Image manipulation rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must not modify individual features within images (no enhancing, obscuring, moving, removing, adding). Image processing such as brightness/contrast adjustments must be applied to every pixel and must not alter information. Cropped images (e.g., gels/blots) should be avoided; where used, full scans must be provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Declare any image processing software and techniques in Methods. Clearly state image grouping and splicing in figure text. Re-use of control images must be declared in legends. AIRA (AI review assistant) is used to detect manipulations; undeclared modifications may lead to requests for original images, rejection, or retraction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review integrity and manipulation prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer review must be objective and honest; intentional deception/manipulation in peer review (falsifying reviewer/editor identities, collusion, fabricated reports, coercive reviewing, undisclosed conflicts, peer review rings) is misconduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anyone aware of attempted manipulation must alert the journal. Investigations follow COPE guidelines and may lead to retraction or revocation of acceptance. Frontiers reserves discretion on what constitutes reasonable evidence of manipulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy on fraudulent contributions and paper mills
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts produced or influenced by paper mills—systematic production of fake or fraudulent academic papers for a fee—are prohibited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must not purchase authorship or outsource research/manuscript production in ways that compromise integrity. Frontiers employs detection technologies and manual checks; authors may be asked for raw data, proof of collaboration, or other assurances. Failure to satisfy queries may lead to rejection, retraction, or institutional reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third-party involvement disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of third-party agents for manuscript writing, submission, or publication processes is discouraged; if used, authors must disclose such involvement in the acknowledgements and detail the extent of their contribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All authors must be included on submission; submitting authors confirm all co-authors are aware and have agreed to their listed contribution. Use of institutional emails is preferable; authors using personal emails may be asked for verification or to link a verified ORCID.

rubrics_metrics.name: Raw data availability and requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Frontiers may request raw/original data during submission checks or formal investigations. Authors are required to provide complete, unaltered datasets in a timely and secure manner when requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow Frontiers' instructions for sharing raw data. Failure to provide requested data may lead to rejection, retraction, or escalation to institutions. Authors are encouraged to contact datapolicy@frontiersin.org for queries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical trial registration and reporting requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: All clinical trials must be prospectively registered in a WHO Registry Network or an ICMJE Approved Registry at or before recruitment of the first subject (applies to trials that began enrolment after 1 July 2005). Retrospectively registered trials will be rejected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include trial registration information in the abstract (unique identifier, registry name, URL). Changes since registration must be reported using CONSERVE guidelines. Randomized trials should follow CONSORT 25-item checklist and include a flow diagram. AI components should follow CONSORT-AI; N-of-1 trials and protocols have respective CONSORT/SPIRIT extensions (SPIRIT-AI). Protocols must be registered and include registry details in abstract.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflicts of interest (COI) disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors, editors, and reviewers must disclose any actual or potential conflicts of interest (personal, financial, professional) that could interfere with objective peer review, decision-making, or publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: COIs should be declared during submission (a statement is automatically generated). Authors should answer provided prompts to identify potential COIs. Templates for commercial affiliations and funding statements are recommended. Undisclosed COIs discovered after publication may lead to action per COPE guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: COI considerations for editors and reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors and reviewers must assess potential conflicts before accepting assignments, including family relationships, recent collaborations, institutional affiliations, financial ties, supervisory/student relationships, and other professional overlaps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should decline assignments if close professional relationships exist that could affect objectivity. Handling editors must recuse themselves from involvement with submissions where conflicts exist; conflicts should be declared in statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission of manuscripts by Frontiers editors or employees
rubrics_metrics.description: Frontiers editors may submit manuscripts but must recuse themselves from peer review, editorial handling, and decision-making for their own articles. Employees submitting manuscripts must notify the research integrity team and recuse from processing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions by editors will be handled by another editor and follow the same single-blind peer review. Editors must list their Frontiers appointment in COI statements. Employee submissions must include a COI statement confirming non-participation in peer review and processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding disclosure requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: All funding sources (including grant numbers) must be declared in the funding section of the manuscript. The role of funders must be stated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frontiers publishes open access under CC-BY. Funding data is submitted to the Open Funder Registry. Recommended templates for declaring employer/funder involvement are provided (e.g., whether funder was involved in design, data collection, analysis, writing, or decision to publish).

rubrics_metrics.name: Open science and data availability (FAIR data)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are required to make the minimal data set underlying the manuscript available to qualified researchers; data should be FAIR (findable, accessible, interoperable, reusable). Mandatory data types must be deposited in community-supported repositories before publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should indicate in Materials and Methods where materials/protocols are available and preferably upload them to repositories with persistent identifiers. Exceptions for legal/ethical/privacy reasons are allowed and must be declared in the Data Availability Statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of materials and resource identification
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must make study materials (protocols, analytic methods, reagents, software, etc.) available to enable reproduction. Participation in the FORCE11 Resource Identification Initiative is encouraged; cite resources using catalog numbers and RRIDs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If repository deposition is not possible, authors should state materials are available on request. Authors must ensure mandatory data is publicly available prior to publication; post-publication inaccessibility may lead to correction or escalation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions to data sharing
rubrics_metrics.description: Limitations on sharing data are permitted where ethical, legal, or privacy concerns exist (e.g., identifiable human data) or for case reports/series with fewer than three individuals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must state limitations clearly in the Data Availability Statement and ensure data sharing complies with participants' consent and institutional policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human participants ethics and consent
rubrics_metrics.description: Research involving human participants must follow the Declaration of Helsinki and relevant institutional/national guidelines, with prior approval from an appropriate ethics committee and informed written consent from participants (including consent for publication where applicable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must provide ethics committee information in the submission system (which generates an ethics statement for the manuscript). If ethics approval or consent is waived, reasons must be stated; Frontiers may request a waiver letter. Identifying information should be omitted unless scientifically necessary and approved. Written informed consent is required for case reports where participants are identifiable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human organs and transplantation research provenance
rubrics_metrics.description: Research using human organs must follow the Declaration of Istanbul and WHO Guiding Principles; authors must be transparent about organ provenance and ethics oversight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should publicly report procuring institution, location, consent process, and ethics oversight in the ethics statement. Unethical procurement will be investigated and may lead to retraction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research involving vulnerable populations
rubrics_metrics.description: Studies on vulnerable populations may trigger requests for additional documentation (recruitment rationale, consent forms, approved protocol) and require data summarization to avoid individual data disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should be prepared to provide consent forms, approved protocols, and other documentation on request. For such studies, data should not include individual-level identifying details; suggested Data Availability Statement language is provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of identifiable human data and publication consent
rubrics_metrics.description: Nonessential identifiable details must be omitted unless explicit written informed consent for publication is obtained; the determination of what constitutes identifiable data lies with editors and editorial staff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Completed consent forms should be stored by authors/institutions and made available upon request, but not included with the submission. Failure to provide required consent documentation may lead to rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Animal research ethics and welfare
rubrics_metrics.description: Research involving animals must follow relevant institutional, national, and international guidelines and obtain prior ethics approval; Frontiers opposes use of materials sourced via unethical animal welfare practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must provide ethics approval information, follow humane standards, and avoid materials from species associated with unethical sourcing (examples listed include bears, pangolins, tortoises, rhinoceroses). Permits/licenses should be reported in Methods; Frontiers may request provenance information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental reporting (replicates and statistics)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must state in figure legends how many times experiments were performed (generally requiring n=3 as a minimum) and specify the statistical analysis performed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear replication counts and analytical methods in legends/Methods to support reproducibility. Deviations from minimums should be justified and approved by ethics/field norms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusivity in global research and permits/licenses
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors conducting research outside their own country or using biological/cultural resources from other communities should adhere to equitable research partnership principles (e.g., TRUST Code) and report permits/licenses as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include permit/license numbers, date and issuing authority in Methods where required. Be mindful of power/resource differentials and ensure transparent provenance reporting; Frontiers may request documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Name change policy (post-publication)
rubrics_metrics.description: Frontiers provides a process for authors to request name or pronoun changes associated with publications, with options for 'silent' updates or correction notices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests require a form with reason, former/new name, contact info, ORCID, role, list of publications, and preference for silent vs correction update. Frontiers will update records and notify third-party databases but cannot guarantee their updates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrections policy (what qualifies for correction)
rubrics_metrics.description: Corrections may be submitted if a small portion of a reliable publication is misleading, a figure error not altering conclusions exists, statistical errors not altering conclusions, mislabeled figures, incorrect author/contributor lists, or similar limited issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corrections must be submitted through the submission system using provided templates and a clear contribution-to-field statement. Contact production.office@frontiersin.org before submission if the error was introduced during publishing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retractions policy and grounds for retraction
rubrics_metrics.description: Frontiers follows COPE guidelines on retraction. Grounds include unreliable findings due to misconduct or honest error, redundant publication without attribution, major plagiarism, unethical research (missing ethics approval), legal issues, major authorship problems (ghostwriting, sold authorship), politically motivated lack of objectivity, singling out individuals/organizations for attack, faith-based pseudoscience, or extraordinary claims without evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retraction decisions follow internal investigations and may incorporate institutional findings. Retraction statements should be public and linked to the original article. Readers reporting concerns should provide correspondence evidence with authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rebuttals and appeals policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors may submit rebuttals to editor/reviewer feedback or appeals if they believe policies were misapplied, but submissions must provide substantive evidence and comply with professionalism standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeals are not considered if one appeal has already been evaluated, if they lack professionalism (personal attacks), solely argue scope/fit, concern legal complexities requiring legal resources, or fail to provide substantive evidence. Assessment is at the journal's discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complaints and allegations handling (including vexatious complaints)
rubrics_metrics.description: Frontiers handles complaints per COPE guidelines and provides mechanisms for community-driven engagement; complainants may be acknowledged in retraction notices if they consent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vexatious complaints (lacking substance, repetitive without new info, intended to harass, refusing constructive dialogue, or containing unreasonably personal/derogatory content) may be handled outside standard processes, timelines, or communications may be closed to protect editorial operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Territorial neutrality policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Frontiers remains neutral regarding published territorial descriptions, maps, and author affiliations; territorial claims are those of the authors and not necessarily of the publisher or editorial staff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No editorial endorsement of territorial claims is implied; authors' affiliations and claims are their own.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support and contact for policy questions
rubrics_metrics.description: Frontiers provides a help center and support email (support@frontiersin.org) for guidance on using the platform and questions about policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors and readers should consult the help center for platform guidance and contact support or research.integrity@frontiersin.org / datapolicy@frontiersin.org for specific integrity or data queries.
